## Brand Photography Cost in India: A Practical Pricing Guide

Brand photography cost in India can range from roughly ₹10,000 for a focused half-day shoot to ₹1 lakh or more for a larger commercial production. The final photography pricing depends on the photographer’s experience, shoot duration, number of products, location, team size, styling, editing, usage rights and GST.

There is no single rate card that fits every business. A Pune-based clinic, a D2C skincare brand, a school and a national consumer brand may all ask for “brand photography”, but their production requirements are very different.

The useful question is not only, “What does the photographer charge?” It is, “What content do we need, how will we use it, and what production is required to create it?”

## What brand photography includes

Brand photography is planned photography created to represent a business consistently across its marketing channels. It can include people, products, spaces, processes, packaging, customer experiences and behind-the-scenes moments.

It is different from ordering a few attractive photos without a wider content plan. A proper brand photography project normally starts with a brief and ends with a set of edited images that can be used for social media, a website, catalogues, advertisements, presentations and sometimes marketplaces.

### Common types of brand photography

A brand shoot may include one or more of the following:

- Founder and team portraits
- Product photography on plain or coloured backgrounds
- Lifestyle product images
- Product-in-use images
- Social media content
- Website banner images
- Office, clinic, studio or school photographs
- Food and menu photography
- Service process photography
- Packaging and unboxing images
- Event and workshop photography
- Staff-at-work images
- Customer or community stories
- Seasonal campaign images
- E-commerce catalogue images
- Short-form video clips alongside still photographs

For example, a handmade jewellery brand may need clean product images, close-up details, model shots, packaging images and Reels content. A school may need campus photographs, classroom scenes, teacher portraits and activity images. These require different planning, equipment, people and editing.

### Brand photography versus regular social media content

A social media shoot is often designed to create a batch of posts, Stories and Reels. It may be informal, fast-moving and focused on volume.

Brand photography usually has a longer shelf life. The images may be used on the website, brochures, pitch decks, advertisements and printed material. It often requires more attention to composition, brand colours, consistency and licensing.

The two can be combined. A business may use one production day to create high-quality website images as well as vertical content for Instagram and YouTube Shorts.

## Indicative brand photography cost in India

The following ranges are broad market indications, not fixed tariffs. Local rates vary between cities, and the same photographer may price a simple portrait session very differently from a styled product campaign.

| Type of photography project | Broad indicative cost in India | Usually suitable for |
|---|---:|---|
| Short portrait or founder session | ₹8,000–₹25,000 | Founder profiles, small teams, LinkedIn and website |
| Half-day small business shoot | ₹15,000–₹40,000 | A few portraits, workspace images and social content |
| Full-day brand content shoot | ₹30,000–₹80,000 | Website, social media and campaign content |
| Product photography on simple backgrounds | ₹10,000–₹50,000 or per-product pricing | Catalogues, websites and marketplaces |
| Styled product or lifestyle shoot | ₹40,000–₹1.5 lakh or more | D2C, food, fashion, beauty and campaign work |
| Larger commercial production | ₹1 lakh–₹several lakhs | Advertising campaigns and major launches |
| Monthly content production arrangement | Varies by scope | Brands requiring recurring photo and video content |

These figures may exclude GST, travel, studio rental, models, makeup, props, food or product styling, assistants, specialised equipment, retouching and paid usage rights.

A basic shoot in a client’s office can cost less than a product campaign involving a studio, art director, stylist, models and multiple sets. A quote of ₹20,000 and a quote of ₹80,000 may both be reasonable if the deliverables are different.

Some photographers charge by the day. Others quote per product, per image, per setup, per campaign or per deliverable. Ask what pricing method is being used before comparing offers.

### What GST does to the quoted amount

If the photographer or production company is registered for GST, GST may be added to the quoted fee. Ask whether the quote is inclusive or exclusive of GST.

For a business that maintains proper accounts, a GST invoice may be important for records and eligible input tax credit, subject to its own tax position and accountant’s advice. Do not assume that an informal lower quote is cheaper after considering invoice requirements, tax treatment and the risk of unclear deliverables.

## The main factors that affect photography pricing

### Photographer’s experience and specialisation

A photographer who mainly shoots portraits may not price a complex food, jewellery or cosmetic product shoot in the same way. Commercial experience can affect the planning quality, lighting approach, consistency and ability to produce images that work across different formats.

The photographer’s fee may also reflect equipment, assistants, editing time, insurance, studio access, software and business overheads.

For a small organisation, the most expensive photographer is not automatically the best choice. The right fit is someone whose portfolio matches the type of images you need and whose process is clear.

### Number of shooting hours or days

A longer booking generally costs more, but shoot duration alone does not explain the full price. A two-hour session with several complicated setups may require more preparation than a full day of straightforward portraits.

The schedule should include time for:

- Setting up lights and backgrounds
- Preparing products or spaces
- Changing outfits or layouts
- Testing compositions
- Photographing multiple angles
- Reviewing key images
- Packing equipment
- Moving between locations

If the brief includes a large number of products, rushing through the shoot can reduce consistency. It may be more practical to split the work into separate days.

### Number of products, people and setups

Product count is one of the biggest pricing variables. Ten products photographed on a simple white background are a different project from ten products each requiring a separate styled scene.

A quote may change based on:

- Number of products
- Number of final images
- Number of angles per product
- Product size and weight
- Reflective or transparent surfaces
- Assembly requirements
- Number of people appearing in the images
- Number of outfits
- Number of scenes or locations
- Number of background colours
- Amount of styling and retouching

A skincare bottle, a plate of food and a large piece of furniture all require different handling. Fragile, reflective, glossy, transparent or highly detailed products may need more careful lighting and post-production.

### Location and travel

An in-studio shoot may involve a studio rental, while a shoot at your office, shop, school or clinic may involve travel and setup time.

For projects outside the photographer’s city, ask whether the quote includes:

- Travel
- Accommodation
- Local transport
- Equipment transport
- Meals or daily allowances
- Location permits
- Parking and loading charges

In Pune and nearby Maharashtra locations, travel between a client’s office, warehouse and outdoor location can affect the schedule. It is better to list locations in the brief than to add them after the quote is approved.

### Models, makeup and styling

People in the images may include founders, employees, hired models, customers or actors. Each option has different costs and practical considerations.

A professional model may require a separate fee and a usage agreement. Makeup, hair styling and wardrobe styling may also be separate. If employees or customers are photographed, obtain written consent and explain where the images may appear.

Product styling can involve a food stylist, prop stylist, fashion stylist, set designer or art director. These roles are not always necessary, but they can make a significant difference in campaign-led work.

### Editing and retouching

Basic editing may include exposure correction, colour correction, cropping and export in suitable formats. Advanced retouching may include removing dust, correcting product surfaces, smoothing fabric, replacing labels, cleaning backgrounds or compositing multiple images.

Ask how many final edited images are included. A photographer may capture hundreds of frames but deliver only a selected number of edited photographs.

Clarify whether the quote includes:

- Selection or proof gallery
- Basic colour correction
- Background removal
- Detailed retouching
- Image compositing
- Image resizing
- Multiple aspect ratios
- Web-ready compression
- High-resolution files for print
- Raw files

Raw files are not automatically included. Many professionals retain them as part of their workflow. If you need raw files, discuss this before booking.

## Comparing different types of shoots

The right format depends on your marketing priorities.

| Shoot type | Main purpose | Typical production needs | Common pricing pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| Founder and team portraits | Website, LinkedIn, proposals and press | Photographer, lighting, simple location | Session or half-day fee |
| Plain-background product shoot | Catalogue, website and marketplaces | Product preparation, lights, consistent setup | Per product or batch pricing |
| Lifestyle product shoot | Instagram, ads and campaign pages | Models, location, props and styling | Day rate plus production costs |
| Social media content day | Regular posts, Reels and Stories | Shot list, multiple formats and quick changes | Day or monthly content fee |
| Space and service photography | Clinics, schools, offices and agencies | Location preparation and staff coordination | Half-day or full-day fee |
| Campaign production | Product launch or seasonal promotion | Creative direction, crew, models and post-production | Project or campaign quote |

A business often needs more than one type. For example, a clinic may require professional doctor portraits and photographs of its reception, consultation rooms and staff interactions. A D2C brand may need catalogue images for its website and lifestyle photographs for paid social media.

Do not select a shoot type only because it has the lowest initial quote. Choose based on where the images will be used and how long they need to remain useful.

## Usage rights, copyright and ownership

Usage rights are an important part of photography pricing and are often overlooked.

In India, the photographer generally creates the photograph and may hold copyright unless the agreement states otherwise. Paying for a shoot does not always mean that every copyright or usage right has automatically been transferred.

Your agreement should explain:

- Where the images can be used
- Whether use includes social media
- Whether use includes paid advertising
- Whether use includes websites and marketplaces
- Whether use includes print brochures and packaging
- Whether use includes outdoor advertising
- The duration of permitted use
- Geographic limits, if any
- Whether the photographer can display the images in a portfolio
- Whether exclusivity is included
- Whether third-party talent has separate restrictions

A small business may need broad usage for its website, social media, Google Business Profile, brochures and digital advertisements. A national campaign may require more formal licensing, especially if the images feature models, actors or other creative contributors.

If a model is photographed, obtain a model release covering the planned usage. If a customer, child, employee or patient appears, use appropriate consent documentation. Schools and clinics should be particularly careful about consent, privacy and the use of identifiable images.

For medical and wellness businesses, avoid using photographs in ways that imply unsupported treatment claims or guaranteed results. The image itself may be attractive, but the accompanying copy and advertising claim must also be reviewed.

## Content production for social media

Brand photography can create a large library of content, but only if the shoot is planned for the channels where it will be used.

Before the shoot, list the required formats:

- Portrait images for Instagram posts
- Vertical frames for Stories and Reels
- Square or landscape images for websites and marketplaces
- Wide banner images for landing pages
- Cropped images for WhatsApp catalogues
- Thumbnail-friendly photographs for YouTube or blog content

Do not simply crop every landscape photograph into a vertical format. The subject may be cut off, text may not fit, and the composition may become unusable. Ask the photographer to compose important images with the final placement in mind.

A practical content brief can include:

1. The business objective
2. The target customer
3. Key products or services
4. Brand colours and visual references
5. Required scenes
6. People who will appear
7. Platforms where the images will be published
8. Number of final images required
9. Required file formats
10. Delivery dates and review process

For Indian brands, plan around real buying periods rather than generic content calendars. A festive campaign, school admissions period, clinic health camp, restaurant menu update or new product launch may require images several weeks in advance for approval and publishing.

A shoot can also include short video clips for social media. However, still photography and video production have different workflows. If you need Reels, product demonstrations or interviews, list video requirements separately instead of assuming they are included.

## How to evaluate a photography quote

A quote should make the scope easy to understand. Do not compare only the total amount.

### Check the deliverables

Ask how many final edited photographs you will receive and whether selection is included. “Full-day shoot” is not a deliverable by itself.

A useful quote may state the number of products, setups, people, locations, final images and revisions. It should also mention the expected file formats and approximate delivery process without making unrealistic promises.

### Check what is excluded

Important exclusions may include:

- GST
- Travel and accommodation
- Studio charges
- Models
- Makeup and styling
- Props and set materials
- Assistants
- Special equipment
- Detailed retouching
- Video content
- Paid advertising usage
- Printing
- Location permissions
- Product transport

Exclusions are not necessarily a problem. They become a problem when nobody discusses them until the production date.

### Review relevant portfolio work

Look for work similar to your project. A strong wedding portfolio does not necessarily demonstrate product photography ability. A fashion portfolio may not show experience with food, healthcare or institutional environments.

Review consistency, lighting, colour, skin tones, product details and the way the images are framed. Ask whether the portfolio shows the photographer’s own work and whether the examples are comparable to your required style.

### Confirm the approval process

Clarify whether you will receive a proof gallery, how selections will be made and how revisions will be handled. Some projects need one round of reasonable corrections, while advanced retouching or reshoots may be charged separately.

Put important approvals in writing through email or WhatsApp. A written brief reduces confusion when multiple people from the business are involved.

### Understand payment and cancellation terms

Photography projects commonly require an advance to reserve the date. The balance may be due after the shoot or on delivery, depending on the agreement.

Ask about cancellation, postponement, damaged products, weather-dependent outdoor shoots and rescheduling. Businesses should also plan who will approve the images if the founder or marketing manager is unavailable.

## Ways to manage the budget without weakening the result

### Prioritise images by business use

Start with the images that support immediate business needs. A small brand may prioritise product pages, founder photographs and ten social media assets instead of attempting a large campaign.

A clear priority list helps the photographer allocate time properly.

### Prepare products and people in advance

Clean, label and organise products before the shoot. Prepare outfits, props, brand guidelines and location access. Delays during the shoot can increase costs and reduce the number of useful setups.

For food photography, arrange ingredients and serving vessels in advance. For schools and clinics, coordinate staff schedules and ensure rooms are ready.

### Group similar setups

Photographing similar products in one setup is usually more efficient than constantly changing lighting and backgrounds. Group products by size, colour, use case or visual treatment.

This is especially useful for product catalogues and social media batches.

### Use one production day strategically

If you need photographs for a website, social media, Google Business Profile and a brochure, include all those requirements in the initial plan. One well-organised production day may produce more useful material than several unplanned sessions.

This does not mean adding unlimited deliverables to one day. It means using the same setup for related outputs.

### Consider recurring content production

A monthly or quarterly arrangement may suit a brand that needs regular content. It can make planning easier and maintain visual consistency, but the scope should remain specific.

Define the number of shoot days, products, locations, final images, videos, revisions and usage rights. “Unlimited content” is usually too vague to manage well.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the average brand photography cost in India?

There is no reliable single average because the term covers simple portraits, product catalogues and large advertising productions. Small sessions may fall in the lower five-figure range, while styled campaigns and larger productions can reach ₹1 lakh or several lakhs. The quote depends on deliverables, team size, production requirements and usage rights.

### How much does a product photography shoot cost in India?

Simple product photography may be priced per product, per image or as a batch, and can begin in the lower five-figure range for a small catalogue. Styled product shoots cost more because they may involve models, props, locations, art direction and detailed retouching. Request a per-product or per-setup breakdown if you have many products.

### Does brand photography cost include GST?

Not always. Some photographers quote an amount before GST, while others provide a GST-inclusive price. Ask for a proper written quote showing the taxable amount, GST if applicable and the final payable amount.

### Are models, props and makeup included in photography pricing?

They are often separate unless the proposal specifically includes them. Confirm model fees, usage permissions, makeup, wardrobe, props, location hire and styling before approving the project. If someone from your staff or customer group will appear, arrange suitable written consent.

### Do I own the photographs after paying the photographer?

Not automatically in every arrangement. Copyright and usage rights should be addressed in the written agreement. Confirm whether you receive commercial usage rights, whether paid advertising is allowed, whether the photographer can use the images in a portfolio and whether raw files are included.

### How many photos should a small business request?

The right number depends on the channels and publishing frequency. It is better to request a planned set of useful images covering products, people, spaces and formats than to focus only on a large image count. A content calendar and shot list can help you estimate the requirement before requesting quotes.

## Where to Start

Begin with a one-page brief covering your business, audience, products or services, locations, people, platforms, desired style and required deliverables. Separate essential images from optional ideas, then request written proposals from photographers whose portfolios match your category.

Compare the complete scope rather than only the headline fee. Check GST, travel, studio and production costs, editing, usage rights, delivery process, payment terms and cancellation conditions.
